## Summary

The purpose of this supplement is to describe analysis of otolith frequency and size composition for our 9 target prey species from accumulated ADF&G measurements from harvested spotted seal stomachs, as well as a few additional samples from scats obtained during NOAA-AFSC seal captures in the Bering Sea.  This analysis feeds into the overall analysis described in the manuscript  "Trophic Roles of Spotted Seals in the Bering and Chukchi Seas" by Boveng et al. 

In particular, I fit models to otolith data that predict otolith frequency and length as a function of potential predictors.  Candidate predictors include spatial strata (Bering vs. Chukchi), age (pup vs non-pup), and season (winter vs. summer).  The ultimate output
from this analysis is a set of estimates and standard errors of several quantities described in the main manuscript, including

- $\lambda_{rsatk}$: the expected minimum number of fish of species $k$ represented by otoliths found in seals of sex $s$, age class $a$, in region $s$ in season $t$;  

- $\nu_{rsatk}$: the predicted length of otoliths of species $k$ in stomachs of seals with covariates $r$, $s$, $a$, and $t$;

Rather than providing a single, constant values for these parameters, we employ a Bayesian estimation scheme and produce posterior samples for these values.  These can be used in later modeling steps to
propagate uncertainty into the ultimate quantities of interest (e.g., total prey biomass consumed).


## Data sources

The first step is to load our various data sources.  Let's start with the ADF&G data, and do some cleaning up (including combining non-target species into an "Other" category).  There are also about 160 otolith lengths that are missing a seal age; rather than throw these away (data are limited!), let's assign them to be non-pups, which
is the most likely scenario.  In many cases, we'll end up omitting age class as a predictor anyway.

```{r, load1}
  Ot_len_df1 <- read.csv(file="../data/ADFG_SpottedSeals_OtolithsMeasured20220627.csv",header=T)
  Ot_len_df1$SealAgeClass[which(Ot_len_df1$SPEC_NUM %in% c("PL12GAM049","PL12SH052","PL14GAM124"))]="Pup"  #confirmed pups via claw age (Justin Crawford, 5/9 email)
  Ot_len_df1$SealAgeClass[which(Ot_len_df1$SealAgeClass=='')]='NonPup'
  Ot_len_df2 <- read.csv(file="../data/ADFG_SpottedSeals_OtolithsMeasured20230424_PriorityMeasurements.csv",header=T)
  colnames(Ot_len_df2)=colnames(Ot_len_df1)  #slight variation in capitalization in column names
  Ot_len_df = rbind(Ot_len_df1,Ot_len_df2)
  Stomachs_df <- read.csv(file="../data/ADFG_SpottedSeals_StomachContentsData20220705.csv",header=T)
  
  #we need a way to link scientific names to common names in various Excel files
  Species = c("Walleye pollock","Pacific cod","Pacific sand lance","Pacific herring",   
"Pacific capelin","Rainbow smelt","Saffron cod","Arctic cod","Yellowfin sole")  
  Species_to_common = matrix(0,9,2)
  Species_to_common[,2]=Species
  Species_to_common[,1]=c("Gadus chalcogrammus","Gadus macrocephalus","Ammodytes hexapterus", "Clupea pallasii","Mallotus villosus","Osmerus mordax","Eleginus gracilis","Boreogadus saida", "Limanda aspera")
  
  #convert latin to common species for otoliths file
  for(isp in 1:9){
    Which_isp = which(Ot_len_df$FishSpecies==Species_to_common[isp,1])
    Ot_len_df$FishSpecies[Which_isp]=Species_to_common[isp,2]
  }
  
  #standardize species names in stomachs file
  Colnames=colnames(Stomachs_df)
  Colnames[13]="Pacific herring"
  Colnames[14]="Rainbow smelt"
  Colnames[15]="Pacific capelin"
  Colnames[16]="Pacific sand lance"
  #note column 17 is a general 'gadidae' category but there aren't too many of them (166)
  #column 80 is "Limanda.sp" - may need to figure out what to do with these
  Colnames[18]="Arctic cod"
  Colnames[19]="Saffron cod"
  Colnames[20]="Walleye pollock"
  Colnames[21]="Pacific cod"
  Colnames[81]="Yellowfin sole"
  colnames(Stomachs_df)=Colnames
  All_sp = c(12:93)
  Keep_sp = c(13,14,15,16,18,19,20,21,81)
  Other_sp = All_sp[-which(All_sp %in% Keep_sp)]
  Other = rowSums(Stomachs_df[,Other_sp])
  Keep_df = Stomachs_df[,Keep_sp]
  Stomachs_df = Stomachs_df[,1:11]
  Stomachs_df = cbind(Stomachs_df,Keep_df)
  Stomachs_df$Other = Other
  
```

Now, let's load in AFSC scat data and attempt to combine that with our stomachs and otolith length
data frames.  There are a few "unknown" age classes in there (when 
field teams found scat but didn't see the animal).  These are more likely
to be non-pups than pups, so rather than throw those out, we'll just set those to be adults.  Note that not all of the ADFG fields are going to be filled in, but we'll make sure to fill in all fields required for our analysis.

```{r, load2}
  AFSC_data <- read.csv("../data/PEP_Pl_otolength_allspecies.csv")
  AFSC_data$prey_species[which(AFSC_data$prey_species=="Clupea pallasi")]="Clupea pallasii"  #fix typo / alternate spelling
  AFSC_data$Season = "Winter"
  AFSC_data$Season[which(AFSC_data$Month>4)]="Summer"
  #change species to common name, and those not in our target list to "other"
  AFSC_data$prey_species[which(!(AFSC_data$prey_species %in% Species_to_common[,1]))]="Other"
  for(isp in 1:9){
    Which_isp = which(AFSC_data$prey_species==Species_to_common[isp,1])
    if(length(Which_isp)>0)AFSC_data$prey_species[Which_isp]=Species_to_common[isp,2]
  }
  AFSC_data$SealAgeClass[which(AFSC_data$SealAgeClass=="Unknown")]="NonPup"

  #calculate %FO by species
  Unique_spenos = unique(AFSC_data$speno)
  n_seal = length(Unique_spenos)
  Species = unique(AFSC_data$prey_species)
  n_un = length(Species)
  I_species = rep(0,n_un)
  FO = rep(0,n_un)
  for(iseal in 1:n_seal){
    for(ifish in 1:n_un){
      Cur_dat = AFSC_data[which(AFSC_data$speno==Unique_spenos[iseal]),]
      if(Species[ifish] %in% Cur_dat$prey_species)FO[ifish]=FO[ifish]+1
    }
  }
  FO = FO/n_seal*100
  
  FO_df = data.frame("Species"=Species,"FOperc"=FO)
  print(FO_df)
  
  #create otolith length data set in same format as ADFG & merge
  Otolith_AFSC = AFSC_data[which(AFSC_data$prey_species %in% Species_to_common[,2]),]
  Dummy_df = as.data.frame(lapply(Ot_len_df[1,], rep,nrow(Otolith_AFSC)))
  Dummy_df$Location = "AFSC"
  Dummy_df$Measured.by = "AFSC"
  Dummy_df$SealSEX="NA"
  Dummy_df$MonthNumb = Otolith_AFSC$Month
  Dummy_df$SPEC_NUM = Otolith_AFSC$speno
  Dummy_df$SealAgeClass=Otolith_AFSC$SealAgeClass
  Dummy_df$OtolithLength=Otolith_AFSC$oto_length_mm
  Dummy_df$Season = Otolith_AFSC$Season
  Dummy_df$FishSpecies = Otolith_AFSC$prey_species
  Ot_len_df = rbind(Ot_len_df,Dummy_df)

# now to coerce into format for stomach data where
# there is one record per seal
  Unique_spenos = unique(AFSC_data$speno)
  n_unique = length(Unique_spenos)
  Dummy_df = as.data.frame(lapply(Stomachs_df[1,], rep,n_unique))
  Dummy_df$Location = "AFSC"
  Sp_names = colnames(Stomachs_df)[12:21]
  for(iseal in 1:n_unique){
    Cur_data = AFSC_data[which(AFSC_data$speno==Unique_spenos[iseal]),]
    Cur_data$prey_species=factor(Cur_data$prey_species,levels=Sp_names)
    Dummy_df[iseal,"SPEC_NUM"]=Cur_data$speno[1]
    Dummy_df[iseal,"SealAgeClass"]=Cur_data$SealAgeClass[1]
    Dummy_df[iseal,"Region"]="Bering"
    Dummy_df[iseal,"MonthNumb"]=Cur_data$Month[1]
    Dummy_df[iseal,"Season"]=Cur_data$Season[1]
    Dummy_df[iseal,"SealAgeClass"]=Cur_data$SealAgeClass[1]
    Dummy_df[iseal,12:21]=summary(Cur_data$prey_species)
  }
  colnames(Dummy_df)=colnames(Stomachs_df)
  Stomachs_df = rbind(Stomachs_df,Dummy_df)
```

Let's look at the number of otoliths by species:

```{r, species_sum}
  colSums(Stomachs_df[,12:21])
```

By comparison, the number of otoliths measured for the 9 species ("Other" is not measured here) are 

```{r, ot_species_sum}
  tabulate(factor(Ot_len_df$FishSpecies,levels=colnames(Stomachs_df[,12:21])))
```
Rather than look at the total number of otoliths measured, it might also be instructive to 
see how many stomachs those represent.  The notion is that otoliths measured from the same stomach represent subsamples that might result in artificially low variance (if a seal is feeding in schools of same-sized fish for example).  Ideally we would measure otoliths across stomachs, rather than continue to measure otoliths from the same stomach.  Let's 
take a closer look at how many stomachs our measured otoliths are from (by species.


```{r, stomach_species_sum}
  Ot_len_df$IDsp = paste(Ot_len_df$SPEC_NUM,Ot_len_df$FishSpecies)
  Unique_IDsp = unique(Ot_len_df$IDsp)
  First = rep(0,nrow(Ot_len_df))
  for(i in 1:length(Unique_IDsp)){
    Cur_which = which(Ot_len_df$IDsp==Unique_IDsp[i])
    First[Cur_which[1]]=1
  }
  Ind_ot_df = Ot_len_df[which(First==1),]
  tabulate(factor(Ind_ot_df$FishSpecies,levels=colnames(Stomachs_df[,12:21])))
```
This seems sufficient to estimate random effects for individuals, although we'll need to be careful in to avoid confounding among covariate predictors (e.g., age class, season, strata) in some of these situations.  This is probably best handled on a case by case basis.  Let's go through each species, fitting 2 models to each: one for the number of fish represented by otoliths of each species, and a second for the length of otoliths that were measured.  The general strategy will be to conduct model selection with GLMM models in a likelihood framework, and the to "flip the switch" to a Bayesian framework to provide posterior predictions for the number of otoliths and length of otoliths (in mm) for each target prey species.  Before we do that, let's set up some structures for holding posterior distributions:

```{r posterior_setup}
Pred_length = array(0,dim=c(10000,9,2,2,2))  
Pred_otoliths = array(0,dim=c(10000,10,2,2,2))  
#dimensions are posterior replicate, prey species, age class, strata, season 
# note we're using a 10th dimension for species to model counts of non-target ('other') species, but
# we won't have otolith lengths for these
```

### Pacific herring

There are decent sample sizes for herring otoliths, but no samples in winter.  

```{r, herring_stomachs}
  Herring_stomachs = Stomachs_df[which(Stomachs_df[,"Pacific herring"]>0),]
  unique(Herring_stomachs$Season)
```
So, we'll by default omit season as a predictor of otolith length.  Let's explore
the effects of region and seal age class, however.  We'll conduct analysis using the glmmTMB package [@BrooksEtAl2017] in R [@RTeam2022].

```{r, glmm_herring1,message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
  library(glmmTMB)
  herring_df = Ot_len_df[which(Ot_len_df$FishSpecies=="Pacific herring"),]
  herring_glmm = glmmTMB(log(OtolithLength) ~ SealAgeClass+Region+(1|SPEC_NUM),data=herring_df,REML=FALSE)
  summary(herring_glmm)
```
It doesn't look like there is evidence for either age class or a regional effect on herring otolith
lengths.  Let's run a simpler model omitting these and "flip the switch" by using the tmbstan package [@MonnahanKristensen2018] to sample posterior predictions for each parameter.  I'll turn 
off output for this one to keep this document tidy.  I'm also going to cache results
but if this is the first time you've run this code it'll take 20 seconds or so.


```{r, herring_stan1,results=FALSE,message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
  herring_glmm = glmmTMB(log(OtolithLength) ~  (1|SPEC_NUM),data=herring_df,REML=FALSE)
  library(tmbstan)
  set.seed(11111)
  stan_fit = tmbstan(herring_glmm$obj,chains=2,iter=10000)
```

Ignoring random effects for individual seals, we'll extract the intercept and make (log-scale)
predictions of otolith length.  We'll wait until we've processed log-scale predictions for all
species before exponentiating to get real scale predictions (this keeps the code a little tidier).

```{r, herring_post1}
  samples = extract(stan_fit,pars=c("beta"))
  
  Pred_length[,1,,,] = unlist(samples)
  # recall dimensions are posterior replicate, prey species, age class, strata, season   # we're basically duplicating these predictions over age class; winter values (season = 2) were initialized to zero and remain zero
```

As a sanity check, let's plot observed otolith lengths with predictions:

```{r, herring_sanity}
 hist(herring_df$OtolithLength)
 abline(v=mean(exp(unlist(samples))))
```
Our predictions (vertical black line) looks to be in the "meat" of the distribution of observed otoliths.

Let's now fit a model to observed otolith counts (both measured and unmeasured).Since these are count data, we'll use a Poisson distribution.  However, we'll omit random effects for individuals since we'd like data means to "speak for themselves."  Allowing random effects has the tendency of reducing the influence of extreme observations, as when seals eat a lot of one fish type; but in this case, we don't necessarily want to explain those away as outliers.  We'll just fit to data from the "Summer" season since "Winter" has all zero counts for herring, and optimizers have a hard time to that (we'll just set the expected herring count in winter to zero).

```{r, herring_count}
  library(glmmTMB)
  herring_df = Stomachs_df
  herring_df$count = Stomachs_df[,which(colnames(Stomachs_df)=="Pacific herring")]
  herring_df = herring_df[which(herring_df$Season=="Summer"),]
  #herring_glmm = glmmTMB(count ~ SealAgeClass+Region+(1|SPEC_NUM),data=herring_df,family="poisson")
  herring_glmm = glmmTMB(count ~ SealAgeClass+Region,data=herring_df,family="poisson")

  summary(herring_glmm)
```

So, looks like there's evidence for effects of both age class and region now.
Let's fit this model using tmbstan and collect predictions.

```{r, herring_stan2,results=FALSE,cache=TRUE}
  set.seed(11111)
  options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())  #speed things up hopefully
  stan_fit = tmbstan(herring_glmm$obj,chains=2,iter=10000)
  samples = extract(stan_fit,pars=c("beta[1]","beta[2]","beta[3]"))

  Beta = matrix(unlist(samples),10000,3)
  Pred_otoliths[,1,1,1,1] = exp(Beta[,1])  # Bering adult
  Pred_otoliths[,1,2,1,1] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,2])  # Bering pup
  Pred_otoliths[,1,1,2,1] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,3])  # Chukchi adult
  Pred_otoliths[,1,2,2,1] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,2]+Beta[,3])  # Chukchi pup
  # recall dimensions are posterior replicate, prey species, age class, strata, season
```

In this case, the three beta parameters are the intercept, the pup effect, and the chukchi effect, respectively - we've used that knowledge to fill in our posterior prediction array.  Note that since we haven't provided values for winter, they are set to the initialized value (zero), as desired.


### Rainbow smelt

Let's repeat the same 2 GLMMs for rainbow smelt, allowing for more or less parameters 
depending on what the data say.  In this case, otoliths from each age class, season, and strata
are available.  However, models with both region and season failed to converge, likely because 
summer obsevations tend to come from the Chukchi and winter observations tend to come from the Bering.
We'll just use a model with region in it; since few seals are in the Chukchi in the winter anyway, this shouldn't really affect our total consumprion estimates.

```{r, glmm_smelt1}
  library(glmmTMB)
  analysis_df = Ot_len_df[which(Ot_len_df$FishSpecies=="Rainbow smelt"),]
  cur_glmm = glmmTMB(log(OtolithLength) ~ SealAgeClass+Region+(1|SPEC_NUM),data=analysis_df,REML=FALSE)
  summary(cur_glmm)
```
It looks like there is evidence for a region effect on otolith size, and weak evidence for
an age class effect.  Let's just use region in the model for posterior predictions since there
are relatively few observations of pups.

```{r, smelt_stan1,results=FALSE}
  analysis_glmm = glmmTMB(log(OtolithLength) ~   Region+(1|SPEC_NUM),data=analysis_df,REML=FALSE)
  library(tmbstan)
  set.seed(11111)
  stan_fit = tmbstan(analysis_glmm$obj,chains=2,iter=10000)
  
  samples = extract(stan_fit,pars=c("beta[1]","beta[2]"))
  Beta = matrix(unlist(samples),10000,2)

  Pred_length[,2,,1,] = Beta[,1]
  Pred_length[,2,,2,] = Beta[,1]+Beta[,2]
  # recall dimensions are posterior replicate, prey species, age class, strata, season   
```

And now for the count GLMM:

```{r, analysis_count}
  library(glmmTMB)
  analysis_df = Stomachs_df
  analysis_df$count = Stomachs_df[,which(colnames(Stomachs_df)=="Rainbow smelt")]
  #analysis_glmm = glmmTMB(count ~ SealAgeClass+Region+(1|SPEC_NUM),data=analysis_df,family="poisson")
  analysis_glmm = glmmTMB(count ~ SealAgeClass+Region+Season,data=analysis_df,family="poisson")

  summary(analysis_glmm)
```

So, looks like there's evidence for all effects.
Let's fit this model using tmbstan and collect predictions.

```{r, analysis_stan2,results=FALSE,cache=TRUE}
  set.seed(11111)
  stan_fit = tmbstan(analysis_glmm$obj,chains=2,iter=10000)
  samples = extract(stan_fit,pars=c("beta[1]","beta[2]","beta[3]","beta[4]"))

  Beta = matrix(unlist(samples),10000,4)
  Pred_otoliths[,2,1,1,1] = exp(Beta[,1])  # Bering adult - summer
  Pred_otoliths[,2,2,1,1] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,2])  # Bering pup - summer
  Pred_otoliths[,2,1,2,1] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,3])  # Chukchi adult - summer
  Pred_otoliths[,2,2,2,1] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,2]+Beta[,3])  # Chukchi pup - summer
  Pred_otoliths[,2,1,1,2] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,4])  # Bering adult - winter
  Pred_otoliths[,2,2,1,2] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,2]+Beta[,4])  # Bering pup - winter
  Pred_otoliths[,2,1,2,2] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,3]+Beta[,4])  # Chukchi adult - winter
  Pred_otoliths[,2,2,2,2] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,2]+Beta[,3]+Beta[,4])  # Chukchi pup - winter

  # recall dimensions are posterior replicate, prey species, age class, strata, season
```
### Pacific capelin

In this case, otoliths from each age class, season, and strata
are available.  However, models with both region and season failed to converge, likely because 
summer obsevations tend to come from the Chukchi and winter observations tend to come from the Bering.
We'll just use a model with region in it; since few seals are in the Chukchi in the winter anyway, this shouldn't really affect our total consumption estimates.

```{r, glmm_capelin1}
  library(glmmTMB)
  analysis_df = Ot_len_df[which(Ot_len_df$FishSpecies=="Pacific capelin"),]
  cur_glmm = glmmTMB(log(OtolithLength) ~ SealAgeClass+Region+Season+(1|SPEC_NUM),data=analysis_df,REML=FALSE)
  summary(cur_glmm)
```

It doesn't look like there's much evidence for variation in otolith size by any
relevant predictor for capelin, so we'll use an intercept-only model for posterior
prediction.

```{r, capelin_stan1,results=FALSE}
  analysis_glmm = glmmTMB(log(OtolithLength) ~ (1|SPEC_NUM),data=analysis_df,REML=FALSE)
  library(tmbstan)
  set.seed(11111)
  stan_fit = tmbstan(analysis_glmm$obj,chains=2,iter=10000)
  
  samples = extract(stan_fit,pars=c("beta"))
  Beta = unlist(samples)

  Pred_length[,3,,,] = Beta
   # recall dimensions are posterior replicate, prey species, age class, strata, season   
```

And now for the count GLMM:

```{r, analysis_count3}
  library(glmmTMB)
  analysis_df = Stomachs_df
  analysis_df$count = Stomachs_df[,which(colnames(Stomachs_df)=="Pacific capelin")]
  analysis_glmm = glmmTMB(count ~ SealAgeClass+Region+Season,data=analysis_df,family="poisson")
  summary(analysis_glmm)
```
Looks like all predictor variables are relevant, so we will include them in posterior predictions.

```{r, capelin_stan2,results=FALSE,cache=TRUE}
  set.seed(11111)
  stan_fit = tmbstan(analysis_glmm$obj,chains=2,iter=10000)
  samples = extract(stan_fit,pars=c("beta[1]","beta[2]","beta[3]","beta[4]"))

  Beta = matrix(unlist(samples),10000,4)
  Pred_otoliths[,3,1,1,1] = exp(Beta[,1])  # Bering adult - summer
  Pred_otoliths[,3,2,1,1] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,2])  # Bering pup - summer
  Pred_otoliths[,3,1,2,1] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,3])  # Chukchi adult - summer
  Pred_otoliths[,3,2,2,1] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,2]+Beta[,3])  # Chukchi pup - summer
  Pred_otoliths[,3,1,1,2] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,4])  # Bering adult - winter
  Pred_otoliths[,3,2,1,2] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,2]+Beta[,4])  # Bering pup - winter
  Pred_otoliths[,3,1,2,2] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,3]+Beta[,4])  # Chukchi adult - winter
  Pred_otoliths[,3,2,2,2] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,2]+Beta[,3]+Beta[,4])  # Chukchi pup - winter

  # recall dimensions are posterior replicate, prey species, age class, strata, season
```

### Sand lance

```{r, glmm_sl1}
  library(glmmTMB)
  analysis_df = Ot_len_df[which(Ot_len_df$FishSpecies=="Pacific sand lance"),]
  cur_glmm = glmmTMB(log(OtolithLength) ~ SealAgeClass+Region+Season+(1|SPEC_NUM),data=analysis_df,REML=FALSE)
  summary(cur_glmm)
```
We will base posterior predictions for otolith length on a model including the one
'significant' predictor: Region.

```{r, sl_stan1,results=FALSE}
  analysis_glmm = glmmTMB(log(OtolithLength) ~ Region+(1|SPEC_NUM),data=analysis_df,REML=FALSE)
  library(tmbstan)
  set.seed(11111)
  stan_fit = tmbstan(analysis_glmm$obj,chains=2,iter=10000)
  
  samples = extract(stan_fit,pars=c("beta[1]","beta[2]"))
  Beta = matrix(unlist(samples),10000,2)

  Pred_length[,4,,1,] = Beta[,1]
  Pred_length[,4,,2,] = Beta[,1]+Beta[,2]

   # recall dimensions are posterior replicate, prey species, age class, strata, season   
```

And now for the count GLMM:

```{r, analysis_count4}
  library(glmmTMB)
  analysis_df = Stomachs_df
  analysis_df$count = Stomachs_df[,which(colnames(Stomachs_df)=="Pacific sand lance")]
  analysis_glmm = glmmTMB(count ~ SealAgeClass+Region+Season,data=analysis_df,family="poisson")
  summary(analysis_glmm)
```
We'll use all 3 covariates when making predictions:

```{r, sl_stan2,results=FALSE,cache=TRUE}
  set.seed(11111)
  stan_fit = tmbstan(analysis_glmm$obj,chains=2,iter=10000)
  samples = extract(stan_fit,pars=c("beta[1]","beta[2]","beta[3]","beta[4]"))

  Beta = matrix(unlist(samples),10000,4)
  Pred_otoliths[,4,1,1,1] = exp(Beta[,1])  # Bering adult - summer
  Pred_otoliths[,4,2,1,1] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,2])  # Bering pup - summer
  Pred_otoliths[,4,1,2,1] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,3])  # Chukchi adult - summer
  Pred_otoliths[,4,2,2,1] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,2]+Beta[,3])  # Chukchi pup - summer
  Pred_otoliths[,4,1,1,2] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,4])  # Bering adult - winter
  Pred_otoliths[,4,2,1,2] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,2]+Beta[,4])  # Bering pup - winter
  Pred_otoliths[,4,1,2,2] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,3]+Beta[,4])  # Chukchi adult - winter
```

### Walleye pollock

```{r, glmm_wp1}
  library(glmmTMB)
  analysis_df = Ot_len_df[which(Ot_len_df$FishSpecies=="Walleye pollock"),]
  cur_glmm = glmmTMB(log(OtolithLength) ~ SealAgeClass+Region+Season+(1|SPEC_NUM),data=analysis_df,REML=FALSE)
  summary(cur_glmm)
```
It would appear both age class and region are viable predictors of otolith size.  However
there are few samples from the Chukchi Sea, and including this covariate produces highly 
variable  (and often negative) predictions of otolith length.  We'll thus only
include age class for posterior predictions:  

```{r, wp_stan1,results=FALSE}
  analysis_glmm = glmmTMB(log(OtolithLength) ~ SealAgeClass + (1|SPEC_NUM),data=analysis_df,REML=FALSE)
  library(tmbstan)
  set.seed(11111)
  stan_fit = tmbstan(analysis_glmm$obj,chains=2,iter=10000)
  
  samples = extract(stan_fit,pars=c("beta[1]","beta[2]"))
  Beta = matrix(unlist(samples),10000,2)

  Pred_length[,7,1,,] = Beta[,1]
  Pred_length[,7,2,,] = Beta[,1]+Beta[,2]

   # recall dimensions are posterior replicate, prey species, age class, strata, season   
```

### "Other" species

The final thing to do is to run some models investigating the counts of non-target ("other")
species.

```{r, analysis_count10}
  library(glmmTMB)
  analysis_df = Stomachs_df
  analysis_df$count = Stomachs_df[,which(colnames(Stomachs_df)=="Other")]
  analysis_glmm = glmmTMB(count ~ SealAgeClass+Region+Season,data=analysis_df,family="poisson")
  summary(analysis_glmm)
```
We'll use all covariates to make these predictions.

```{r, other,results=FALSE,cache=TRUE}
  set.seed(11111)
  stan_fit = tmbstan(analysis_glmm$obj,chains=2,iter=10000)
  samples = extract(stan_fit,pars=c("beta[1]","beta[2]","beta[3]","beta[4]"))

  Pred_otoliths[,10,2,1,1] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,2])  # Bering pup - summer
  Pred_otoliths[,10,1,2,1] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,3])  # Chukchi adult - summer
  Pred_otoliths[,10,2,2,1] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,2]+Beta[,3])  # Chukchi pup - summer
  Pred_otoliths[,10,1,1,2] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,4])  # Bering adult - winter
  Pred_otoliths[,10,2,1,2] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,2]+Beta[,4])  # Bering pup - winter
  Pred_otoliths[,10,1,2,2] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,3]+Beta[,4])  # Chukchi adult - winter
  Pred_otoliths[,10,2,2,2] = exp(Beta[,1]+Beta[,2]+Beta[,3]+Beta[,4])  # Chukchi pup - winter

  # recall dimensions are posterior replicate, prey species, age class, strata, season
```


## Output 

Finally, we'll exponentiate our otolith length predictions and save posterior output for future use.  We'll also save otolith length data for some future sanity checking.

```{r, output,results=FALSE,cache=TRUE}
  Pred_length = exp(Pred_length)
  Meta = "Posterior distributions for predicted otolith lengths and counts occurring in spotted seal stomachs from the Bering and Chukchi Seas.  Dimensions of each array are posterior replicate, prey species, age class (Adult/Pup), strata (Bering/Chukchi), and season (Summer/Winter).  The order of prey species is pacific herring, rainbow smelt, capelin, sand lance, Arctic cod, saffron cod, walleye pollock, pacific cod, and yellowfin sole.  The 10th entry for otolith counts is for non-target/other species.  Otolith lengths are in mm."
  Otolith_posteriors = list("Pred_otoliths"=Pred_otoliths,"Pred_length"=Pred_length,Meta=Meta)
  save(Otolith_posteriors, file="../data/otolith_posteriors.RData")
  save(Ot_len_df,file="../data/Ot_len_df.RData")
```
